누구.forms: subject: 누가 (not 누구가) · object: 누구를 (누굴) · whose: 누구의
누구.x: Who is this person in the photo?
누구.t: With 가, 누구 becomes 누가: 누가 왔어요? (Who came?)

하나.forms: native · counting things, hours, age · before a counter: 한 (한 개, 한 시)
하나.t: Before a counter 하나 shortens to 한: 한 명, 한 살, 한 시.

다음.forms: 다음이 · 다음에 · 다음 주 · 다음 달
다음.x: Get off at the next stop.
다음.e: 다음 주 = next week, 다음 달 = next month.
다음.t: 다음에 봐요! 'See you next time!' is a common goodbye.

하늘.x: The autumn sky is really blue.

준비하다.e: 준비 (preparation) + 하다 (do); 준비됐어요? = Are you ready?

짜다.x: The soup is a little salty.
짜다.e: 짜요 = it's salty. A different 짜다 means 'to squeeze'.

취소하다.x: I was sick, so I canceled my hotel reservation.

회화.ex: 요즘 영어 회화 수업을 듣고 있어요.
회화.x: These days I'm taking an English conversation class.
회화.t: 회화 is language-class conversation; an everyday chat is 대화 or 이야기.

회화.ex: 이 전시회에서는 조선 시대 회화를 볼 수 있어요.
회화.x: At this exhibition, you can see paintings from the Joseon era.
회화.t: Homonym warning: 회화 (會話) means 'conversation', as in 영어 회화.

시다.ex: 이 레몬은 너무 셔서 먹을 수 없어요.
시다.x: This lemon is so sour I can't eat it.
시다.e: 시 + 어요 shortens to 셔요; 신 김치 is sour, well-aged kimchi.

신부.ex: 하얀 드레스를 입은 신부가 정말 아름다워요.
신부.x: The bride in the white dress is really beautiful.
신부.t: Homonym warning: 신부 also means 'Catholic priest', written with different characters.

이제.ex: 이제 한국 음식을 잘 먹을 수 있어요.
이제.x: Now I can eat Korean food well.
이제.e: 이 'this' + 제 'time', the same 제 as in 언제 'when'.
이제.t: 이제 suggests a change from before; 지금 simply means the present moment.

올해.x: This year I really want to learn to drive.
올해.e: Native 해 'year'; unlike 작년 and 내년, it is not Sino-Korean.

연말.x: At the end of the year, I spend time with my family.

반짝반짝.x: The stars are twinkling in the night sky.
반짝반짝.e: 의태어 (manner word) for small lights flickering on and off. Its dark-vowel partner 번쩍번쩍 is for big, strong flashes, like lightning.
반짝반짝.t: Pronounced [반짝빤짝]: the second ㅂ becomes tense after ㄱ. Verbs: 반짝이다 and 반짝거리다 'to twinkle, to sparkle'.

소화.ex: 밥을 너무 빨리 먹으면 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
소화.x: If you eat too fast, you won't digest well.
소화.e: Literally 'dissolve and transform' — food breaking down.
소화.t: 소화가 안 돼요 is the everyday way to say 'I have indigestion.'

스트레스.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 스트레스를 많이 받아요.
스트레스.x: I've had a lot of work lately, so I'm really stressed.
스트레스.e: From English 'stress' — one English syllable becomes four Korean ones.
스트레스.t: You 받다 (receive) stress and 풀다 (untie) it: 노래방에서 스트레스를 풀어요.

예절.x: Table manners differ a little from country to country.
예절.t: A key table rule: wait until the oldest person starts eating before you pick up your spoon.

의논하다.x: I talked over the move with my family.
의논하다.t: 의 at the start of a word is pronounced [의]; casual speech often blurs it toward [이].

바라보다.m: to look at, to gaze at; to view
바라보다.x: We drank coffee while gazing at the ocean.
바라보다.e: Probably 바라- 'toward, hoping' + 보다 'to see': to look toward.
rel: to look up at, to stare

유지.x: I exercise every day to stay healthy.
유지.e: Literally 'tie and hold' — keep things as they are.

알바.x: I worked a part-time job at a convenience store during vacation.
알바.e: Short for 아르바이트, from German 'Arbeit' (work); in Korea it means a part-time job.
알바.t: 알바 is casual; use 아르바이트 in writing or formal situations.

투자하다.x: Lots of people invest in stocks these days.

예금.x: Every month I deposit part of my salary in the bank.

질투하다.ex: 동생은 엄마가 언니만 예뻐해서 언니를 질투해요.
질투하다.x: My little sister is jealous because Mom only dotes on our older sister.
질투하다.t: 질투 sounds negative and resentful, while 부럽다 is light envy or admiration.

놀이기구.x: I went on five rides at the amusement park.
놀이기구.t: Pronounced [노리기구]: the ㄹ links into the next syllable. Rides are 'ridden': 놀이기구를 타다.

히히.x: My little brother played a prank and giggled 'hee-hee'.
히히.e: 의성어 (sound word) for a cheeky, mischievous giggle, typical of children.
히히.t: Adults use it mostly in texts to sound playful or soften a tease.

빙글빙글.x: The children hold hands and spin round and round.
빙글빙글.e: Manner word (의태어) for something turning smoothly again and again. Bright-vowel 뱅글뱅글 describes smaller things spinning.
빙글빙글.t: 머리가 빙글빙글 돌아요 'My head is spinning' describes dizziness; 빙글빙글 웃다 is a soft, ongoing smile.

효율.ex: 새 프로그램을 쓰니까 일의 효율이 높아졌어요.
효율.x: Using the new program made our work more efficient.
효율.t: 효율 often describes systems and resources; 능률 describes how well people work.

조교.ex: 과제에 대해 궁금한 점은 조교에게 물어보세요.
조교.x: Ask the TA if you have questions about the assignment.

그야말로.e: 그 'that' + -야 emphasis + 말로 'in words': 'that, in the truest words'.
그야말로.t: Adds strong emphasis, like 'nothing short of': 그야말로 최고예요 'It's truly the best.'

불구하다.forms: Mostly as connectors: N에도 불구하고 · -(으)ㅁ에도 불구하고
불구하다.m: despite, in spite of (lit. to disregard)
불구하다.ex: 비가 오는데도 불구하고 많은 사람이 모였어요.
불구하다.x: Despite the rain, many people gathered.
불구하다.e: Literally 'not restrained by'; something doesn't stop the result.
불구하다.t: Almost always appears as 에도 불구하고 'in spite of'; it rarely stands alone.

대비하다.m: to prepare for, to get ready for (a future event or risk)
대비하다.ex: 겨울에 대비해서 따뜻한 옷을 미리 샀어요.
대비하다.x: I bought warm clothes in advance to prepare for winter.
대비하다.e: Literally 'prepare to face'; homonym warning: 대비 also means 'contrast'.
대비하다.t: Pattern: N에 대비하다 'prepare for N', as in 시험에 대비하다 or 노후에 대비하다.

빠뜨리다.m: to drop (into); to leave out, omit; to lose (something)
빠뜨리다.x: I accidentally dropped my phone in the toilet.
빠뜨리다.e: 빠지다 'to fall in; to be missing' + -뜨리다, which makes it forceful.
빠뜨리다.t: 빠트리다 is also standard and means the same thing.
rel: to fall in; to be missing

일깨우다.ex: 그 사고는 우리에게 안전의 중요성을 일깨워 주었어요.
일깨우다.x: That accident made us realize the importance of safety.
일깨우다.e: Built on 깨우다 'to wake someone up': waking up someone's awareness.

좌우하다.ex: 첫인상이 면접 결과를 좌우할 수 있어요.
좌우하다.x: A first impression can decide the outcome of an interview.
좌우하다.e: Literally 'left and right': steering something either way.

애매하다.ex: 약속 시간이 애매해서 점심을 먹기가 어려워요.
애매하다.x: The meeting time is awkward, so it's hard to fit in lunch.
애매하다.e: Literally 'dim and dark' — not clear either way.
애매하다.t: Everyday speech: 좀 애매해요 means 'it's hard to say' or 'it's neither here nor there'.

몸 둘 바를 모르다.forms: 몸 둘 바를 몰라요 · 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요 · 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요 (르 irregular)
몸 둘 바를 모르다.m: to not know what to do with oneself (from embarrassment or gratitude)
몸 둘 바를 모르다.ex: 칭찬을 너무 많이 해 주셔서 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요.
몸 둘 바를 모르다.x: You're praising me so much that I don't know what to say.
몸 둘 바를 모르다.e: Literally 'to not know where to put one's body.'
몸 둘 바를 모르다.t: A humble, polite reply to big praise or kindness, usually as 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요.

수치.x: My blood pressure numbers dropped a lot from last month.
수치.t: Homonym: 수치 meaning 'shame' appears in 수치심, 'sense of shame'.

째깍째깍.ex: 조용한 방에 시계 소리만 째깍째깍 들려요.
째깍째깍.x: In the quiet room, all you can hear is the clock going tick-tock.
째깍째깍.e: 의성어 (sound word) for the small, crisp tick of a clock's second hand.
째깍째깍.t: The verb 째깍거리다 is common: 시계가 째깍거려요. 똑딱똑딱 is another way to say tick-tock.

성큼성큼.ex: 키 큰 형이 앞에서 성큼성큼 걸어가요.
성큼성큼.x: My tall older brother is striding ahead with long steps.
성큼성큼.e: 의태어 (manner word) for walking with long, confident steps.
성큼성큼.t: Single 성큼 also means 'all of a sudden, by a big step': 봄이 성큼 다가왔어요 'Spring has suddenly arrived.'

동글동글.x: Grandma rolled the rice cakes into little round balls.
동글동글.e: 의태어 (manner word) built on 동글다 'round'. Its dark-vowel pair 둥글둥글 is bigger, and also describes an easygoing person.
동글동글.t: 동글동글하다 is a cute way to describe a round face or eyes: 얼굴이 동글동글해요.

비리.x: The company president's wrongdoing was reported in the media.
비리.e: Literally 'against reason', that is, not right.
비리.t: Common in news: 비리를 저지르다 (commit wrongdoing) and 비리가 드러나다 (come to light).

말끔하다.ex: 그는 면접 날 정장을 입고 말끔하게 차려입었어요.
말끔하다.x: He dressed up neatly in a suit on the day of the interview.
말끔하다.e: Close cousin of 깔끔하다 'neat'; adverb 말끔히 means 'completely, without a trace'.

어쩔 수 없이.forms: 어쩔 수 없이 ~았/었어요 · 어쩔 수 없어요
어쩔 수 없이.m: with no choice, inevitably, against one's will
어쩔 수 없이.ex: 버스가 끊겨서 어쩔 수 없이 택시를 탔어요.
어쩔 수 없이.x: The buses had stopped running, so I had no choice but to take a taxi.
어쩔 수 없이.e: Literally 'without a way to do (어쩌다) anything'.
어쩔 수 없이.t: As a predicate: 어쩔 수 없어요 'It can't be helped.'

기점.m: starting point; (as ~을 기점으로) from, beginning with
기점.ex: 그 사건을 기점으로 회사가 크게 바뀌었어요.
기점.x: Starting with that incident, the company changed dramatically.
기점.t: Key pattern: N을/를 기점으로 'from N on, with N as the starting point'.

근간.ex: 중소기업은 우리 국가 경제의 근간이라고 할 수 있습니다.
근간.x: Small and medium businesses can be called the backbone of our national economy.
근간.e: Literally 'root and trunk' of a tree — the parts that hold it up.

사퇴.m: resignation, stepping down; withdrawal (from a race)
사퇴.ex: 장관은 책임을 지고 사퇴 의사를 밝혔습니다.
사퇴.x: The minister took responsibility and announced his intention to resign.
사퇴.t: 사퇴 is typical for politicians and candidates; for ordinary workers, 퇴사 (leaving a company) is used.

배점.m: points allotted (to a question), score allocation
배점.ex: 이 문제는 배점이 높으니까 꼭 풀어야 해요.
배점.x: This question is worth a lot of points, so you have to solve it.

멸시하다.m: to look down on, to disdain
멸시하다.ex: 가난하다는 이유로 사람을 멸시하면 안 돼요.
멸시하다.x: You shouldn't look down on people just because they're poor.

화근.m: root of trouble, source of misfortune
화근.ex: 그때 한 거짓말이 결국 화근이 되었어요.
화근.x: The lie I told back then eventually became the root of all the trouble.
화근.t: Usually used with 되다: X이/가 화근이 되다 means 'X turned out to be the cause of the trouble.'
rel: to remove the source of trouble

덮어씌우다.m: to cover (something over); to pin the blame on, frame
덮어씌우다.x: He pinned his own mistake on his coworker.
덮어씌우다.e: 덮다 'to cover' + 씌우다 'to put on': covering someone with blame.
덮어씌우다.t: Common pattern: 죄를 덮어씌우다 or 누명을 씌우다, 'to falsely accuse someone.'

변론.ex: 변호사는 법정에서 피고인을 위해 열심히 변론했습니다.
변론.x: The lawyer argued hard for the defendant in court.
변론.t: Pronounced [별론] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

법률행위.x: Contracts and wills are typical examples of juristic acts.
법률행위.e: 법률 'law' plus 행위 'act': an act meant to create legal effects.
법률행위.t: Pronounced [범뉼행위] — nasalization plus ㄹ becoming ㄴ.

긴축재정.x: The government implemented austerity to reduce its budget deficit.

분산투자.ex: 위험을 줄이려면 분산투자를 하는 것이 좋아요.
분산투자.x: To reduce risk, it's good to diversify your investments.
분산투자.t: Korean has the same proverb: 달걀을 한 바구니에 담지 마라 — don't put all your eggs in one basket.

목적론.x: Aristotle explained nature from a teleological perspective.
목적론.e: Literally 'goal theory'; 목적 pictures the eye fixed on a target.
목적론.t: Pronounced [목쩡논]: ㄱ before ㄹ makes both sounds nasal.

윤회.x: Both Buddhism and Hinduism believe in reincarnation.
윤회.e: Literally 'wheel turning': life and death spinning round and round.

해제.m: introductory notes (on a text), bibliographical commentary
해제.ex: 책 뒤에 실린 해제를 읽으면 작품을 더 깊이 이해할 수 있어요.
해제.x: Reading the notes at the back of the book helps you understand the work more deeply.
해제.e: Literally 'explaining the title'; a homonym 해제 means lifting a ban or alert.

졸문.x: It's a clumsy piece of writing, but I'd welcome your feedback.
졸문.e: Literally 'clumsy writing' — often a humble word for one's own writing.

근묵자흑.m: you become like the company you keep
근묵자흑.ex: 근묵자흑이라고, 나쁜 친구는 멀리하는 게 좋아요.
근묵자흑.x: You become like the company you keep, so it's best to avoid bad friends.
근묵자흑.e: Literally 'whoever stays near ink turns black'.

파기하다.m: to break (a contract); to destroy (documents); to overturn (a ruling)
파기하다.x: The company unilaterally broke the contract.
파기하다.t: In court news, 원심 파기 means 'reversal of the lower court's ruling'.

유려하다.m: flowing, fluent, graceful (of writing or style)
유려하다.x: His sentences are flowing and beautiful.

무참하다.x: Their dreams were brutally crushed by the war.
무참하다.e: Literally 'beyond misery'; the 'no' syllable intensifies rather than negates.
무참하다.t: Mostly as 무참히: 무참히 짓밟히다/무너지다 'to be crushed mercilessly'.

새록새록.ex: 사진을 보니 옛 추억이 새록새록 떠올라요.
새록새록.x: Looking at the photos, old memories keep coming back fresh.
새록새록.e: Probably built on 새 'new' — things keep feeling new.

연원.ex: 이 풍습의 연원은 삼국 시대로 거슬러 올라갑니다.
연원.x: The origin of this custom goes back to the Three Kingdoms period.
연원.e: Literally 'deep pool and spring' — where water begins.
연원.t: Collocation: 연원이 ~(으)로 거슬러 올라가다 'to date back to ~'.
